summary: This work demonstrates hierarchical simulation of adiabatic quantum flux parametron (AQFP) gates in Keysight ADS using symbolically defined devices (SDD) to model Josephson junctions with arbitrary current-phase relations. The non-sinusoidal $I(\phi)$ characteristics of SNS and weak-link junctions are shown to substantially alter AQFP switching speed, output current swing ($\pm 20$ µA for SIS versus $\pm 40$ µA for SNS), and timing margins.
motivation: AQFP logic gates promise low-dissipation cryogenic control circuits for superconducting qubit multiplexing, but their performance depends sensitively on Josephson junction quality, necessitating quantitative understanding of how deviations from ideal SIS junctions affect gate dynamics.
method: SDD models of SIS, SNS, and weak-link junctions with different current-phase relations $I/I_c = \sum_{n=1}^{N} \alpha_n \sin(n\phi)$ were implemented in ADS and used to simulate AQFP buffers ($I_{c1} = I_{c2} = 50$ µA, $L_1 = L_2 = 2.64$ pH) and a 3-stage shift register with phase-shifted clocks.
result: SNS junctions produced doubled output current swing ($\pm 40$ µA) but slower switching than SIS or weak-link junctions; weak links achieved the sharpest switching with smallest current margin, while SIS junctions exhibited intermediate behavior due to their symmetric sinusoidal relation.
